# Psalm 146 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Hallelujah! Let my whole being praise the LORD!

**2** I will praise the LORD my entire life; I will sing praises to my God as long as I breathe.

**3** Don't put your trust in powerful people — in any human being who can't save you.

**4** When they die, they return to the ground, and on that very day all their plans evaporate.

**5** But how happy is the person whose help is the God of Jacob — whose hope is in the LORD their God!

**6** He made heaven and earth, the sea, and everything in them. He keeps every promise forever.

**7** He brings justice to the oppressed and feeds the hungry. The LORD frees prisoners.

**8** The LORD gives sight to the blind. The LORD lifts up those who are crushed. The LORD loves those who do right.

**9** The LORD protects foreigners. He supports orphans and widows. But he twists the plans of the wicked.

**10** The LORD reigns forever! Your God, Zion, rules through every generation! Hallelujah!

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **146:3-4**: Don't trust powerful people. Why? Because they die. And when they die, their plans die with them. Every four years this verse becomes profoundly relevant.

- **146:7-9**: This is God's résumé of action: justice, food, freedom, sight, support, love, protection. These aren't just theological ideas — they're things God actually does for real people in real need.

— PNEUMA
